key_insight: A domain‑invariant semi‑supervised segmentation framework that automatically discovers latent domains in mixed‑center medical image sets and aligns them using a Clustered Maximum Mean Discrepancy (C‑MMD) loss, removing the need for explicit domain labels.
problem_solved: Addresses scarce expert annotations and severe, unknown multi‑scanner/center domain gaps in medical image segmentation where data come from multiple unlabeled domains (mixed‑domain setting).
method: Automatically cluster samples to infer latent domains from mixed labeled and unlabeled medical images.
Apply Clustered Maximum Mean Discrepancy (C‑MMD) to align feature distributions across the inferred clusters, creating domain‑invariant representations.
Train a semi‑supervised segmentation model jointly with the C‑MMD alignment and unlabeled‑data supervision (e.g., pseudo‑labels or consistency regularization).
impact: Enables more robust, generalizable segmentation models across hospitals and scanners with fewer annotations, easing real‑world deployment and reducing annotation costs for medical AI projects.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data input (mixed labeled + unlabeled) → clustering (latent domains) → C‑MMD alignment → segmentation network
t‑SNE/UMAP plots showing feature distributions before vs after C‑MMD alignment (clusters merge across domains)
Bar/line chart: segmentation accuracy vs % labeled data comparing baseline, single‑domain DA, and the proposed method
Qualitative montage: example medical images with segmentation overlays before and after domain‑invariant training
paper_title: Domain-invariant Mixed-domain Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation with Clustered Maximum Mean Discrepancy Alignment
paper_authors: Ba-Thinh Lam, Thanh-Huy Nguyen, Hoang-Thien Nguyen, Quang-Khai Bui-Tran, Nguyen Lan Vi Vu
